title: Resilient Strategies- Tailwinds in Left-Tail Scenarios - Pablo Calderini

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Resilient Strategies- Tailwinds in Left-Tail Scenarios - Pablo Calderini.docx

speakers: Pablo Calderini (Graham Capital Management, macro portfolio manager)
summary: Graham Capital talk (mid-2024): central-bank regime history, left-tail risks, stock-bond correlation drivers and the case for adding discretionary/systematic macro to a 60/40 portfolio.

coverage.note: central bank put regime history; 2022 tightening; Q1 2024 equity rally
inflation risk; equity valuations/AI; cocoa; stock-bond correlation history
stock-bond correlation drivers; macro inputs; 2022 positioning
FX view; dynamic equity exposure; drawdown record

completeness_estimate: 0.82 - first reader caught the headline themes, statistics and tables (central-bank regimes, vol, stock-bond correlation, drawdown record, 60/40 results); missed supporting mechanisms (post-COVID policy sequence, Middle East reading, macro style and vol reduction reasons) and misordered the Q1 2024 rally versus the Fed pivot.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: there was always a central bank willing to take action, ease monetary policy to help the situation
claims.claim: In 2010-2020 the central-bank put made bad news bullish for assets, compressing volatility and making life difficult for macro traders.
claims.conditions: QE era, vol suppressed

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: now the central banks could not, not only they could not accommodate that shock, you had a bad shock for growth and stocks
claims.claim: The 2022 inflation shock broke the central-bank put: banks had to tighten (fastest hike cycle ex-Volcker, largest real rate rise), so stocks fell and macro funds profited.
claims.conditions: when inflation prevents easing

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: They had a four information ratio in Q1, 2000 this year, right?
claims.claim: In Q1 2024 equities rose in a straight line from about 4200 to 5200 on the S&P with an information ratio near 4 versus a normal 0.6-0.7, after the Fed turned dovish in December and volatility hit lows.
claims.conditions: dovish global central banks, decent growth

correction.issue: Says equities rallied 'after the Fed turned dovish in December'. Pablo says the S&P bottomed around 4200 at the end of October and rose 1000 points in four months, and that the rally started before the Fed pivot (markets were reading it ahead of time).
correction.fix: From a late-October 2023 low near 4200 the S&P rose about 1000 points in four months, in a near straight line with an information ratio near 4 in Q1 2024 versus a normal 0.6-0.7, with volatility at lows; the rally began before the Fed's December dovish pivot, so markets anticipated it.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: if you want to look at one barometer for global volatility uncertainty, that's it really
claims.claim: VIX (13 low, about 16), MOVE (about 100) and JPM FX vol all sat at low levels, which contrasts with elevated geopolitical and economic risk.
claims.indicator: VIX, MOVE index, JPM FX vol index
claims.conditions: low vol with high tail risk

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: that would be the biggest shock financial markets has ever seen
claims.claim: A China-Taiwan blockade or invasion would be the largest financial shock ever, comparable to or worse than March 2020; Ukraine and Middle East add smaller tail risks.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: core PCE, right? So it's not only the PCE index, but it's the one that excludes the most volatile items
claims.claim: The Fed's 2% target is on core PCE (excluding energy and food), so core PCE is the inflation series to follow.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: The 4% core PCE inflation annualizes to 5%.
claims.claim: Core PCE monthly prints annualising to about 5% (inflation bounced in early 2024) would trigger another Fed hike; this is a main left-tail risk though not the base case.
claims.conditions: if inflation stays high

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: Valuations for equities, I don't think that that is that much of a complete concern because earnings have increased as well
claims.claim: Equity gains came partly from P/E expansion but earnings are growing strongly and AI companies make real profits, unlike 2002 internet firms; still, after sharp rises left tails arise from shocks.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: prices have moved up four times or more in the last few months
claims.claim: Cocoa quadrupled in months on West African weather extremes (rain then drought), a possible sign of climate-change commodity volatility.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: if you look at the chart of the 100 years stock bond correlation
claims.claim: Over 100 years the stock-bond correlation averages about zero but is almost never near zero, living in a bimodal distribution; the 60/40 relies on a negative correlation.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: between 1960 and 1995, really stock bond correlation was very, very positive, reaching sometimes level of 60% correlation
claims.claim: Stock-bond correlation was strongly positive (up to 60%) from 1960 to 1995 and negative for the last 20 years.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: when the main driver of macroeconomic shocks is growth, right? So inflation is not a concern, then the stock bond correlation tends to be negative
claims.claim: Stock-bond correlation is negative when growth shocks dominate (rates fall on bad news) and positive when inflation is high (bad shocks hit both stocks and bonds).
claims.conditions: inflation regime

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: And we are back to a world of positive correlation.
claims.claim: In 2024 stock-bond correlation had turned positive again, a bad development for 60/40 asset owners, and depends on inflation.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: NVIDIA became something very relevant because even though it looks like a micro issue, it really became a macro issue
claims.claim: Macro funds track anything that moves global markets, e.g. Nvidia as an AI proxy that drove equities.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: in 2022, we were extremely short interest rates globally, right? Under the conviction that rates needed to replace four, 500 basis points
claims.claim: In 2022 the macro book was short rates, short stocks and commodities and long the dollar because the Fed was the most aggressive; in 2024 conviction was lower but still short rates with US curve steepeners and short Japanese rates.
claims.direction: short global rates, short equities, long USD
claims.conditions: when central banks tighten

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: We are long the dollar because we are seeing this very strong US economy performing really well that will make the Fed less able to cut rates
claims.claim: A strong US economy limits Fed cuts while the ECB cuts independently, supporting a long dollar view.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: one thing that we do really well is to change our position in equities, risk on risk of assets, depending on the regime
claims.claim: The macro index is positively correlated to equities in good markets and cuts or goes short in bad ones (conditional/negative correlation), complementing equity-heavy portfolios.
claims.indicator: macro index correlation to MSCI World
claims.conditions: equity drawdowns

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: equities went down 24%, then in macro made 6.7%.
claims.claim: In equity drawdowns macro gained: 1990 recession (MSCI -24%, macro +6.7%), 2000-02 (-46%, +13%), 2008 (-54%, positive), 2022 (-25%, macro +10%).
claims.indicator: macro hedge fund index in MSCI World drawdowns
claims.conditions: equity bear markets

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: It's not the same as buying equity puts that for sure will do well if equities go down.
claims.claim: Macro is not guaranteed to hedge: Q1 2020 COVID sell-off saw macro down about 2%, unlike equity puts.
claims.conditions: fast shock without time to reposition

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: It's more what it's called conditional correlation. If equities are doing terribly, very likely will be short.
claims.claim: Macro offers conditional correlation: low to negative correlation to equities and bonds when they perform badly, but not always low.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: returns, the annualized returns on the portfolio go from 6.7 with no macro to 7.2 with 20% macro
claims.claim: Adding 20% macro to a 60/40 (1990-2023) raised return 6.7 to 7.2%, cut vol 10.2 to 8.7%, lifted Sharpe 0.65 to 0.83, cut max drawdown 36% to 29% and cut equity beta 0.7 to 0.55.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: after so many years of loose monetary policy, massively loose fiscal policy, finally we had this inflation shock, which was a game changer
claims.claim: The COVID shock was external but triggered a massive central-bank reaction and asset inflation; after years of loose monetary and fiscal policy, goods and consumer inflation arrived in 2022, so loose policy sowed the inflation shock that ended the 'bad news is good news' regime.
claims.indicator: central bank easing, fiscal stimulus, inflation
claims.conditions: Applies to the 2020-22 sequence.
claims.testable: partly - historical sequence, causal link is argued

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: every developed central bank really became what's called dovish
claims.claim: In December 2023 the Fed and nearly every developed central bank (all except the BoJ) turned dovish while growth was decent, a benign backdrop for equities, and markets had already rallied in anticipation of it.
claims.conditions: Growth must be decent for easing to be bullish rather than a recession signal.
claims.testable: yes - equity returns around the pivot

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: neither the Iranian attack nor the Israeli defense were true acts of war, was more like to calm down their own local populations
claims.claim: Pablo reads the April 2024 Iran-Israel exchange as largely symbolic, giving a short-term truce, but a line was crossed (direct attacks from each country's territory) and small war games can go wrong; a single mass-casualty strike would have forced a much harder Israeli response.
claims.conditions: Depends on miscalculation or casualties; the truce is short-term.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: a 1.2 peak headline PCE, that annualizes at 15%
claims.claim: The mid-2022 inflation peak was extreme on a monthly basis: headline PCE peaked at 1.2% in a month (15% annualised) and core near 8% annualised, in a world used to 2% inflation and deflation fears.
claims.conditions: Data point on the size of the 2022 inflation shock.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: We are really, really focused on global central banks, monetary policy, something that we can anticipate well. When central banks are in action, we typically perform really, really well.
claims.claim: A macro book's key inputs are growth, inflation and the Fed and other central banks; central-bank policy is the part it can anticipate well, and it performs best when central banks are actively changing policy.
claims.direction: macro returns higher when central banks act
claims.conditions: Weaker when central banks are on hold.
claims.testable: partly - macro index returns vs policy-change episodes

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: We have very low correlation to asset classes in the long run, but on any given day, we proactively seek to have exposure to markets to profit from changes
claims.claim: Discretionary macro sits between passive/long-only tactical allocation and pure arbitrage: it has low long-run correlation to asset classes but takes active directional exposures day to day.
claims.indicator: macro style positioning vs asset classes
claims.conditions: Style description by a manager.
claims.testable: yes - correlation of macro index to asset classes

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: rates needed to replace four, 500 basis points. When that happens, usually stocks go down.
claims.claim: In 2022 the macro book paired short global rates (on the view that rates needed to rise 400-500bp) with short stocks and short commodities and long the dollar, because large rate rises usually push stocks down and the Fed was the most aggressive central bank.
claims.direction: short rates, short stocks, long USD
claims.conditions: A regime of aggressive central-bank tightening.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: we are good at forecasting bad markets for equities. And typically we would get short in anticipation and during those markets
claims.claim: A macro manager claims no long or short bias but skill at anticipating bad equity markets, going short in anticipation and during them, and shifting risk-on exposure by regime.
claims.direction: short before and during equity sell-offs
claims.conditions: Self-reported; the 2020 sell-off shows it fails sometimes.
claims.testable: yes - macro index conditional correlation to equities

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: This is the index we made more than double that.
claims.claim: In the 2022 equity drawdown (-25%) the macro index returned about 10% on average while Graham's own macro program made more than double that.
claims.indicator: Graham macro vs macro hedge fund index 2022
claims.conditions: Manager-specific record from a firm presentation.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: macro trades at the lower roll than equities. Secondly, it has almost zero correlation
claims.claim: Adding macro lowers portfolio volatility for two reasons: the macro index runs at lower volatility than equities and has almost zero correlation to the portfolio, so the Sharpe ratio rises (return up while volatility falls).
claims.conditions: Applies to a 60/40 portfolio with 10-20% macro.
claims.testable: yes - from index volatility and correlation
